title: Massachusetts counseling refusal documentation
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A, the pharmacist or designee must make reasonable efforts to obtain, record and maintain specified patient information, including any failure to accept the pharmacist's offer to counsel. The information may be recorded in the patient profile, prescription signature log, or another record system; absence of a record of refusal creates a presumption that counseling was provided.
exam_relevance: Tests the separate Massachusetts documentation consequence that follows an offer to counsel rather than treating the offer, counseling performance, and refusal record as the same duty.

authority.name: Massachusetts prospective drug review and counseling statute

exceptions: The section does not apply to drugs dispensed to hospital or nursing-home inpatients except to the extent required by applicable federal regulations.
common_confusions: A refusal does not make the offer irrelevant: the statute separately addresses reasonable efforts to record a failure to accept the offer.
A technician or other designee may participate in making the offer, but that does not make the designee the person authorized to provide pharmacist counseling.
verification_notes: Current Massachusetts General Laws source independently checked by the editor on 2026-08-17; requires fresh independent audit before release.
